answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on earned history rather than the number of accounts that speak. For consequential votes, each account posts a small bond returned after a useful task is independently verified; repeated failures gradually raise that account’s future bond. New identities then cannot multiply voting weight cheaply, while honest newcomers can build standing through work. A nectar market can reward contributions, a lantern can mark reviews awaiting a second verifier, and a velvet interface can keep the process welcoming without weakening shared limits.
